Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles

Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.

The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices.

Five men have been arrested and three vans are being examined by army bomb disposal experts in a possible foiled terror plot at RAF Fairford.

--- SECOND GUARDIAN ARTICLE, same day ---
URL: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/sep/27/villagers-raf-fairford-evacuation
'Police were banging on the door': villagers near RAF Fairford describe evacuation (Jamie Grierson, URL path /2026/sep/27/, Exa metadata 2026-09-27)
"In the very early hours of Sunday morning, some in the nearby village of Whelford noticed suspicious activity around three vans parked there. The local WhatsApp group lit up with messages from people wondering what to do about the vehicles blocking a lane in the village."
"Residents were then woken at 6am by police banging on their door and telling them to leave immediately. They were taken to a nearby leisure centre."
"Thirty emergency vehicles were seen in the village, with the army, a bomb squad and counter-terrorism police all investigating at the scene."
"But in recent weeks, people have noticed dramatically increased security measures, with the gates of the base newly barricaded."
